description: How this factory's own pinned dependencies are kept current — its tooling, and the manifests under assets/ that every generated project starts from.

Nothing here runs by itself: this repository lives on a Gitea forge, so it needs a self-hosted Renovate run — a scheduled workflow on the forge's own runner, or a cron job — with a token that may open pull requests. On GitHub it would be the Renovate app instead. See docs/maintaining.md.

An npm bump under assets/ is only half a change. The committed locks in assets/languages/typescript/locks/ and assets/frontends/react-vite/locks/ have no package.json beside them — they are built per axis combination by `make locks` — so `make check-locks` goes red on the pull request until `make locks` has been run on it and the result committed. That is the intended workflow, not a defect: the lock and its manifest have to be produced together.

What Renovate cannot see here, stated rather than left to be discovered: the per-feature npm versions in src/slipwai/project/languages/typescript.py's PACKAGE_ADDITIONS (fastify, pg, node-pg-migrate and their types), the build-tool pins in src/slipwai/images.py (pack, ko, the Paketo builders, the Jib base), the toolchain versions in src/slipwai/backends.py, and .github/runner/versions.env. Those are Python source and an env file, not manifests; they are bumped by hand, and docs/backend-obligations.md section 4 says who owns each choice.

pip_requirements.description: The factory's three requirement files, which the default pattern would miss: it matches a prefix before the word and not the suffix after it.

packageRules.description: The manifests a generated TypeScript service and browser app start from. A pull request here is finished when `make locks` has been run on it and the regenerated locks are in the same commit.
The Go modules a generated Go service starts from, with the checksums that come with them; `make locks` rebuilds these too.
The factory's own lint, type-check, build and publish tooling.
The actions this repository's own workflows use.

A major is a piece of work here rather than a bump: an asset's dependency reaching a new major changes what every project generated afterwards is given, forever, and nobody is asked again. It waits on the dependency dashboard until somebody asks for it.
